name: Penang
summary: George Town's UNESCO heritage streets, murals and clan jetties, Kek Lok Si temple on the hill, and Malaysia's best hawker food.

months.note: One of the driest months; Chinese New Year often falls in late Jan or Feb and fills George Town.
Driest month; Chinese New Year and Chap Goh Meh bring crowds and higher room prices.
Hot and mostly dry; a good time to walk the heritage streets.
Showers pick up in the afternoons; mornings are best for walking.
A short drier spell between the rains.
Afternoon showers; school holidays bring regional visitors.
Very wet; quietest time for hotels.
Wettest month; plan indoor stops like museums and cafes.
Still wet as the northeast monsoon starts.
Rain eases; year-end holidays fill hotels.

tips.title: Fill in the MDAC before you fly
tips.body: Travellers entering Malaysia must submit a Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) before travel, and airlines may ask for it at check-in. Use only the official site, imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac/main. The Malaysian Immigration website lists who is exempt.

tips.title: 90-day visa-free stay for UK visitors
tips.body: British tourists are normally allowed 90 days on arrival. Other nationalities should check their own allowance. Work, study or longer stays need a visa arranged before travel.

tips.title: Six months' passport validity
tips.body: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months after your arrival date, undamaged and with no missing pages.

tips.title: Do not overstay
tips.body: Even a short overstay can lead to a fine, detention, deportation at your own cost or a ban on returning. Check the stay granted on your entry record.

tips.title: Possible drug test on arrival
tips.body: Authorities may require a urine test on arrival. You can be penalised even if the drug was taken in a country where it is legal.

tips.title: Declare cash of US$10,000 or more
tips.body: You must declare cash or travellers' cheques worth US$10,000 or more. Taking ringgit worth US$10,000 or more into or out of Malaysia needs prior approval.

tips.title: Yellow fever certificate if arriving from a risk country
tips.body: You need a yellow fever vaccination certificate if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. This does not apply to direct flights from most of Europe or North America.

tips.title: Cover up at mosques and temples
tips.body: Cover shoulders and knees and take off your shoes before going in.

tips.title: Tipping is optional
tips.body: Restaurants often add a service charge, so tipping isn't expected. RM2 to RM5 for hotel housekeeping is a kind extra.

tips.title: Free CAT bus around George Town
tips.body: The free CAT hop-on bus loops George Town between Weld Quay and KOMTAR bus terminals every 10 to 15 minutes, from about 6 am to midnight.

tips.title: Bus 203 or 204 to Kek Lok Si
tips.body: Rapid Penang buses 203 and 204 run from KOMTAR to Air Itam in about 50 minutes for RM2. A Grab is about RM11.

tips.title: Penang Hill funicular costs RM40 return
tips.body: Visitors without a Malaysian MyKad pay RM40 return per adult on the normal lane, or RM80 on the express lane. The funicular runs from 6:30 am.

places.name: Reunion Carnarvon
places.blurb: Small hotel on Lebuh Carnarvon in George Town's heritage zone, opened 2024.

places.name: The Frame Guesthouse
places.blurb: Guesthouse with dorms, capsules and private rooms in a three-storey heritage shophouse on Lebuh Chulia, once a frame maker's shop.

places.name: Hotel Penaga
places.blurb: Heritage boutique hotel made from a row of pre-war terrace houses at Jalan Hutton and Lebuh Clarke.

places.name: George Town street art
places.blurb: Murals and iron-rod cartoons across the UNESCO heritage zone, including Ernest Zacharevic's 2012 pieces like Children on Bicycle on Armenian Street.

places.name: Chew Jetty
places.blurb: The largest of George Town's Chinese clan jetties: stilt houses on wooden walkways over the water, still lived in by the Chew clan.

places.name: Antarabangsa Enterprise
places.blurb: Kerbside bar attached to a liquor shop on Lorong Stewart, known as the cheapest place in George Town for drinks. Daily 5 pm to 2 am.

places.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
places.blurb: Malaysia's largest Buddhist temple, on a hillside in Air Itam, with the seven-tier Ban Po Thar pagoda and a giant Kuan Yin statue.
places.tip: Open 8:30 am to 5:30 pm. The temple is free; the pagoda is RM2 and the inclined lift to Kuan Yin RM2 each way.

places.name: Penang Air Itam Laksa
places.blurb: Famous assam laksa stall on Jalan Pasar near Kek Lok Si: sour fish broth with thick rice noodles.
places.tip: Saturday and Sunday only, 11 am to 6 pm, and closed one weekend a month.

places.name: Farlim Night Market
places.blurb: Wednesday-night pasar malam at Medan Angsana in Farlim, with street food and stalls.
places.tip: Wednesdays only, from about 5 or 6:30 pm to 11 pm.

places.name: Bus from George Town to Air Itam
places.blurb: Rapid Penang buses 203 and 204 from KOMTAR to Air Itam, about 50 minutes.

itineraries.title: Penang in 3 days
itineraries.creator: bucketlistly
itineraries.summary: The last leg of Pete's 10 days in Malaysia: George Town's street art and clan jetties, cheap beers, then Kek Lok Si with a bowl of laksa and the Farlim night market.

items.name: Reunion Carnarvon
items.note: Creator's pick. Or The Frame Guesthouse (dorms) or Hotel Penaga (high-end). Base yourself in George Town.

items.name: George Town street art
items.note: Hunt for the murals, like Brother & Sister on a Swing.

items.name: Bus to Air Itam
items.note: A direct bus runs from George Town to Kek Lok Si.

items.name: Kek Lok Si Temple
items.priceNote: temple free; RM2 for the pagoda

items.name: Laksa near Kek Lok Si
items.note: Try the most delicious laksa there.

items.name: Farlim Night Market
items.note: Go in the evening and try all the street food Penang has to offer. Runs on Wednesdays.
